conventional.policy_description: Expand CTC to \$3,600/\$3,000 per child, fully refundable. Based on 2021 ARP expansion.

credibility.no_band_reason: no pre-registered row scores a refundable credit
credibility.own_row_caption: Calibrated to reproduce $1.60T (CBO/JCT 2021) — agreement is by construction, not an independent test.
limitations: holdout labels follow the locked post-2026-05-02 regression protocol; they are not retroactive historical out-of-sample claims.
No pre-registered out-of-sample row scores a policy of this class, so this model's accuracy on one has not been measured.
Credit eligibility and refundability are modeled with synthetic tax units rather than CPS ASEC microdata.
Interactions with SALT, AMT, and filing-status heterogeneity remain approximated in the current household tax module.

The module's annual for this benchmark is -$160.0B, the carried $1,600B target divided by exactly ten, so the by-construction error tests x/10 x 10 == x and nothing else. Read the leave-one-out row instead: run_loo.py derives this case per unit from the CPS microdata and never touches the annual. The row is kept rather than deleted so the tautology stays visible - deleting a benchmark to improve a tier mean is the failure mode pre-registration exists to forbid.
The $1,600B is a rounded secondhand figure attributed to 'CBO/JCT 2021' with no transcribed table row behind it, so the residual on the derived side is measured against a target of unknown precision.
credibility.caption: No out-of-sample band: no pre-registered row scores a refundable credit. The 44 pre-registered Tier 1 rows are the only tier that measures this model's accuracy, and none of them scores a policy of this kind.
